turns.content: Hello, my boiler has broken down and I have already signed an 8 500 € quote to replace it before winter. How can I finance these works?

Your boiler replacement project (8 500 €) is indeed a works financing need, and a suitable offer exists for this type of need.

**Recommendation: the Expresso Loan**

It is an amortising personal loan, not allocated to a specific purchase, which matches a works project perfectly. It covers your amount (from 1 000 €), over a term of 12 to 84 months, with an indicative APR of 5.49% — a rate that depends on your file and is not a firm offer. Monthly payments are adjustable and early repayment is possible.

**Point to watch on affordability**

Your current situation already shows an existing loan monthly payment of 956 €, for a debt-to-income ratio of around 20% and an average savings capacity of around 928 €/month. Your available savings amount to 14 695 €. A new monthly payment would add to your existing charge: the project remains feasible, but it is important to check that the monthly payment remains compatible with your budget. Using part of your savings would reduce the amount to borrow and therefore the cost of the loan — without a down payment being required.

**Concrete next step**

To obtain a personalised estimate of your monthly payment and the total cost, use the official simulator: [URL|Simulate my Expresso Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/credit-conso-expresso]

If you would like to refine your file, I can also direct you to an advisor: [URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]

Thank you for these explanations. If I decide to use some of my savings to reduce the amount borrowed, does that change anything for the timeframe to obtain the financing? Because I would like the works to be done before winter.

Using part of your savings does not, in itself, change the processing time of the file: the amount borrowed is lower, but the steps (review, issue of the offer, withdrawal period, fund release) remain the same. It can, however, indirectly smooth the file, because a smaller financing need is generally simpler to analyse.

On your schedule constraint, the key point is the fund release timeframe: the Expresso Loan states a minimum of 8 days after approval. It is this timeframe, more than the level of savings used, that determines whether the works can be done before winter. I would therefore advise starting the application without delay, rather than waiting to decide how much savings to use.

On affordability, your situation remains consistent: your current debt-to-income ratio and your available savings leave room, and reducing the amount borrowed makes for a more comfortable file. The project therefore looks affordable, provided the exact monthly payment is validated.

To choose between "savings used" and "amount borrowed", keep in mind that savings reduce the cost of the loan but eat into your reserve, whereas the loan preserves your savings at the price of a higher total cost. The precise pricing (monthly payment, total cost) comes from the official simulator: [URL|Simulate my Expresso Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/credit-conso-expresso]

If you want to secure the schedule before winter, an advisor can support you in building the file: [URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
